subject: english
prompt_en: Name two things the speaker wants to do for her friends.
prompt_hi: Do cheezein batao jo speaker apne friends ke liye karna chahti hai.
answer: Any two: give her very best; do more than share their hopes and plans; help make their wishes come true; love them the way they are

subject: english
prompt_en: The speaker wants to see her friends with her heart. What does that mean?
prompt_hi: Speaker apne dosto ko 'heart' se dekhna chahti hai. Iska kya matlab hai?
answer: To understand her friends through feelings and love, not only by how they look from outside

subject: english
prompt_en: The speaker says she will not judge her friends 'from afar'. What does that mean, and what will she do instead?
prompt_hi: Speaker kehti hai woh apne dosto ko 'from afar' judge nahi karegi. Iska kya matlab hai, aur uske badle woh kya karegi?
answer: Not to judge friends from a distance without knowing them; instead she will love her friends the way they are

subject: english
prompt_en: Which one is a prayer? A: 'I hope we win the race tomorrow.' B: 'May my friend get well soon.' Why?
prompt_hi: Kaunsa prayer hai? A: 'I hope we win the race tomorrow.' B: 'May my friend get well soon.' Kyun?
answer: B, because it begins with 'May' and asks for something good for someone else

subject: english
prompt_en: Explain to your younger sibling what kind of friend the speaker of the poem wants to be.
prompt_hi: Apne chhote bhai-behen ko samjhao ki poem ki speaker kis tarah ki dost banna chahti hai.
answer: A friend who gives her best, helps her friends' wishes come true, understands them with her heart and loves them as they are

subject: english

answer: grateful and thankful

subject: english
prompt_en: Write two lines of your own friend's prayer: one starting with 'May' and one starting with 'Let me'.

answer: Two correct lines with plain verbs, e.g. 'May my friends always be happy. Let me cheer for them when they lose.'

subject: english
prompt_en: Your friend tells you a secret: she is scared of the dark. A classmate asks you what she said. As a caring friend, what do you do? Is there a kind of secret you should not keep?
prompt_hi: Tumhari dost tumhe ek secret batati hai: use andhere se dar lagta hai. Ek classmate poochta hai usne kya kaha. Ek caring dost ke roop mein tum kya karoge? Kya koi aisa secret bhi hota hai jo nahi chhupana chahiye?
answer: Keep it safe and politely refuse to tell; but if a secret means someone is being hurt or is in danger, tell a trusted adult

subject: english

prompt_hi: Hindi mein 'sachcha dost' kehte hain. Ise English mein kaise bolenge?

subject: english
prompt_en: What was special about the chair that grandfather gave Mario?
prompt_hi: Dada ne Mario ko jo chair di, usmein kya khaas tha?
answer: It was invisible: nobody could see it

subject: english
prompt_en: Put these in order: (a) Mario 'sat' in mid-air. (b) Grandfather brought the chair from the attic. (c) Mario fell again and again while classmates laughed. (d) The children ate fruit chaat with grandpa.
prompt_hi: In events ko sahi order mein lagao: (a) Mario 'sat' in mid-air. (b) Grandfather brought the chair from the attic. (c) Mario fell again and again while classmates laughed. (d) The children ate fruit chaat with grandpa.
answer: b, c, a, d

subject: english
prompt_en: When Mario finally 'sat' in mid-air, what was really holding him up?
prompt_hi: Jab Mario aakhir hawa mein 'baitha', use asal mein kya ya kaun sambhaal raha tha?
answer: His three true friends, Guneet, Asma and Deepa, held him up so he would not fall

subject: english
prompt_en: Each time Mario fell, he said it was only 'a slight technical problem' and tried again. What does this show about him?
prompt_hi: Har baar girne par Mario kehta tha ki bas 'a slight technical problem' hai aur phir try karta tha. Isse Mario ke baare mein kya pata chalta hai?
answer: He was determined (strong-willed) and would not give up

subject: english
prompt_en: Contrast the three friends with the other classmates during the chair test.
prompt_hi: Chair test ke time 3 dosto aur baaki classmates mein kya farak tha?
answer: The three friends held Mario up so he would not fall; the others laughed and enjoyed each fall

subject: english
prompt_en: Why was grandfather's idea of the invisible chair clever?
prompt_hi: Dada ka invisible chair wala idea clever kyun tha?
answer: Mario was sure to fall, so the test showed who cared and helped him and who enjoyed his bad luck

subject: english
prompt_en: Explain the message of 'The Chair' to your younger cousin in two sentences.
prompt_hi: Apne chhote cousin ko 'The Chair' ka message do sentences mein samjhao.
answer: True friends care for us and help us when we fall. Someone who laughs at our bad luck is not a real friend.

subject: english
prompt_en: Mario joins a new tuition class and soon has many 'friends' there. After this story, predict how he might find out who his real friends are.
prompt_hi: Mario ek nayi tuition class join karta hai aur wahan jaldi bahut 'dost' ban jaate hain. Is story ke baad, predict karo woh asli dost kaise pehchanega?
answer: He might use the chair test again, or watch who helps him when he is in trouble; those who care and help are his real friends

subject: english
prompt_en: Someone you met online says, 'Let's be best friends! Send me your photos and your school's name.' Using the story's idea of a true friend, is this a true friend? What should you do?
prompt_hi: Online mile kisi ne kaha, 'Let's be best friends! Send me your photos and your school's name.' Story ke 'true friend' wale idea se socho, kya ye sachcha dost hai? Tum kya karoge?
answer: No; a true friend cares for you and does not ask for private things. Do not send anything, and tell a parent or trusted adult.

subject: english
prompt_en: What does the Sanskrit name 'Arishta' mean, and who gave the tree the name 'Neem'?
prompt_hi: Sanskrit naam 'Arishta' ka matlab kya hai, aur 'Neem' naam kisne diya?
answer: 'The one who cures diseases'; the Iranians gave it the name 'Neem'

subject: english
prompt_en: Tell a friend three uses of the neem tree from the dialogue, in your own words.
prompt_hi: Ek dost ko dialogue se neem ke 3 upyog apne shabdon mein batao.
answer: Any three: twigs clean teeth; leaves protect clothes and help in measles; bark medicine for cough; flower kajal for itchy eyes; seed powder keeps locusts, termites and mosquitoes away and protects stored grain; neem oil goes into soap and toothpaste; neem wood is safe from termites

subject: english
prompt_en: Turn the dialogue into a table: part of the tree → use. What goes next to 'flowers', and what next to 'seeds'?
prompt_hi: Dialogue ko ek table mein badlo: ped ka hissa → upyog. 'Flowers' ke aage kya likhoge, aur 'seeds' ke aage kya?
answer: Flowers → kajal for itchy eyes; seeds → powder that stops locusts and termites (and mosquitoes, and protects grain)

subject: english
prompt_en: When Amber's brother had measles, why did the doctor ask the family to put neem leaves on his bed?
prompt_hi: Jab Amber ke bhai ko measles hua, doctor ne uske bistar par neem ke patte rakhne ko kyun kaha?
answer: Because neem leaves destroy germs and stop them from breeding, and they give comfort from the itching

subject: english
